question: Which Pi resource-discovery exclusions reduce fresh exact-extension Worker bootstrap time without removing unrelated configured resources or weakening exact extension selection?
prediction: Disabling individual resource classes can reduce RPC-ready time, but a Worker launch must retain unrelated configured extensions and Skills. Bundling the exact extension can reduce TypeScript loader work, but it cannot prove Worker Session binding or Task delivery by itself.
invariants: Every case loads exactly one Pi Team Bright extension from its explicit source.
The current exact-launch case retains a separately configured unrelated extension and Skill.
A globally discovered duplicate Pi Team Bright extension causes registration failure; suppressing all discovery is not an acceptable production remedy.
RPC readiness, Session binding, interactive readiness, and Task delivery are separate outcomes.
data_dag: isolated fixture profile -> child Pi process -> probe lifecycle records -> redacted raw sample
raw samples -> successful-only nearest-rank summaries -> invariant assessment -> candidate ranking
verification: Fresh isolated PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and session directory per sample.
Probe records extension factory, session_start, and resources_discover lifecycle events.
The runner fails if an expected unrelated extension or Skill is absent from the current exact-discovery case.
The runner proves the duplicate exact-extension case fails rather than masking it.
limits: This harness uses Pi RPC mode, not a terminal carrier, so it cannot observe Herdr interactive_ready.
It does not construct a durable Team Membership. Exact Worker binding and first Task delivery are recorded as not attempted rather than inferred.
cleanup: The runner removes every temporary fixture and kills every child it starts. The committed result contains only redacted records.
